arxiv-2101-07444.description: Abstract . We consider convex, black-box functions f f with additive or multiplicative noise with a high-dimensional parameter space Λ \Lambda and a data space 𝒟 \mathcal{D} of lower dimension, where ∇ f \nabla f exists, but may be inaccessible.

arxiv-2103-11764.title: Transfer learning from High-Resource to Low-Resource Language Improves Speech Affect Recognition Classification Accuracy
arxiv-2103-11764.creator: Sara Durrani, Umair Arshad
arxiv-2103-11764.description: Abstract Speech Affect Recognition is a problem of extracting emotional affects from audio data. Low resource languages corpora are rear and affect recognition is a difficult task in cross-corpus settings. We present an approach in which the model is trained on high resource language and fine-tune to recognize affects in low resource language.

arxiv-2108-12043.title: Learning Disentangled Representations in the Imaging Domain Journal: Medical Image Analysis
arxiv-2108-12043.creator: Xiao Liu, Pedro Sanchez, Spyridon Thermos, Alison Q. O’Neil, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris
arxiv-2108-12043.description: Abstract Disentangled representation learning has been proposed as an approach to learning general representations even in the absence of, or with limited, supervision. A good general representation can be fine-tuned for new target tasks using modest amounts of data, or used directly in unseen domains achieving remarkable performance in the corresponding task.

arxiv-2203-12348.title: Characteristics of small protoplanetary disc warps in kinematic observations 2021 Characteristics of small protoplanetary disc warps in kinematic observations – B
arxiv-2203-12348.creator: Alison K. Young, Richard Alexander, Giovanni Rosotti, Christophe Pinte
arxiv-2203-12348.description: Abstract Many circumstellar discs appear to have misaligned central regions that give rise to shadows seen in scattered light observations. Small warps ( < 20 ∘ <20^{\circ} misalignment) are probably more common but are also more difficult to detect than the large misalignments studied previously.

arxiv-2308-06527.title: With a Little Help from the Authors: Reproducing Human Evaluation of an MT Error Detector
arxiv-2308-06527.creator: Ondřej Plátek, Mateusz Lango, Ondřej Dušek
arxiv-2308-06527.description: Abstract This work presents our efforts to reproduce the results of the human evaluation experiment presented in the paper of Vamvas and Sennrich 2022 , which evaluated an automatic system detecting over- and undertranslations (translations containing more or less information than the original) in machine translation (MT) outputs.

arxiv-2408-00690.title: Improving Text Embeddings for Smaller Language Models Using Contrastive Fine-tuning
arxiv-2408-00690.creator: Trapoom Ukarapol, Zhicheng Lee, Amy Xin
arxiv-2408-00690.description: Abstract While Large Language Models show remarkable performance in natural language understanding, their resource-intensive nature makes them less accessible. In contrast, smaller language models such as MiniCPM offer more sustainable scalability, but often underperform without specialized optimization. In this paper, we explore the enhancement of smaller language models through the improvement of their text embeddings.

arxiv-2510-04032.title: Small Language Models for Emergency Departments Decision Support: A Benchmark Study
arxiv-2510-04032.creator: Zirui Wang 1 , Jiajun Wu 1 , Braden Teitge 2 , Jessalyn Holodinsky 3 , Steve Drew 1
arxiv-2510-04032.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly popular in medical domains to assist physicians with a variety of clinical and operational tasks. Given the fast-paced and high-stakes environment of emergency departments (EDs), small language models (SLMs), characterized by a reduction in parameter count compared to LLMs, offer significant potential due to their inherent reasoning capability and efficient performance.

arxiv-2511-11408.title: Effects of Early-Universe Inhomogeneity on Bubble Formation: Primordial Black Holes as an Extreme Case
arxiv-2511-11408.creator: Yijie Chang, Haowen Deng, Yefeng Wang, Ran Ding, Shihang Tang, Fa Peng Huang
arxiv-2511-11408.description: Abstract Our early Universe is not perfectly homogeneous and it may contain some inhomogeneous sources, which might distort the local spacetime and modify the bubble nucleation rate. Taking the primordial black hole as an extreme example, we investigate the bubble nucleation rate of a first-order phase transition in the vicinity of primordial black holes or other primordial gravitational sources.

arxiv-2512-17324.title: Vertical velocities in quasigeostrophic laboratory vortices
arxiv-2512-17324.creator: Marine Aulnette, Michael Le Bars, Patrice Le Gal
arxiv-2512-17324.description: Abstract In the present study, we test the predictions of the ω \omega -Equation against laboratory experiments with direct measurements of the vertical velocity w. Our results are further completed through the use of theoretical models of oceanic vortices, with the aim of helping oceanographers in better quantifying regions of upwelling and downwelling in the ocean.

pmc-10604652.title: The Relationship between TNF-a, IL-35, VEGF and Cutaneous Microvascular Dysfunction in Young Patients with Uncomplicated Type 1 Diabetes
pmc-10604652.creator: Jolanta Neubauer-Geryk, Melanie Wielicka, Małgorzata Myśliwiec, Katarzyna Zorena, Leszek Bieniaszewski, Paweł Maga
pmc-10604652.description: The aim of this study was to analyze the relationship between immunological markers and the dysfunction of cutaneous microcirculation in young patients with type 1 diabetes. The study group consisted of 46 young patients with type 1 diabetes and no associated complications. Microvascular function was assessed with the use of nail fold capillaroscopy before and after implementing post-occlusive reactive hyperemia.

pmc-10700109.title: A chromosome-level reference genome for the common octopus, Octopus vulgaris (Cuvier, 1797)
pmc-10700109.creator: Dalila Destanović, Darrin T Schultz, Ruth Styfhals, Fernando Cruz, Jèssica Gómez-Garrido, Marta Gut, Ivo Gut, Graziano Fiorito, Oleg Simakov, Tyler S Alioto, Giovanna Ponte, Eve Seuntjens, P Campbell
pmc-10700109.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Cephalopods are emerging animal models and include iconic species for studying the link between genomic innovations and physiological and behavioral complexities. Coleoid cephalopods possess the largest nervous system among invertebrates, both for cell counts and brain-to-body ratio. Octopus vulgaris has been at the center of a long-standing tradition of research into diverse aspects of cephalopod biology, including behavioral and neural plasticity, learning and memory recall, regeneration, and sophisticated cognition. However, no chromosome-scale genome assembly was available for O.

pmc-11330961.title: Adapting the Parent Connector program for caregivers of adults with SMI: the Family Connector experience
pmc-11330961.creator: Paige E Cervantes, Charlotte Gendler, Lori Markowitz, Meggin Rose, Priscilla Shorter, Sally Mason, Tanya Hernandez, Kimberly E Hoagwood
pmc-11330961.description: Caregivers play an essential role in the recovery of their adult loved ones with serious mental illness (SMI). Promoting caregiver empowerment and well-being is critical but has often been overlooked. Family peer interventions are well-suited to fill this need; however, research is limited supporting their use with caregivers of adults with SMI.

pmc-12431357.title: Advancing Remote Life Sensing for Search and Rescue: A Novel Framework for Precise Vital Signs Detection via Airborne UWB Radar
pmc-12431357.creator: Yu Jing, Yili Yan, Zhao Li, Fugui Qi, Tao Lei, Jianqi Wang, Guohua Lu
pmc-12431357.description: Highlights What are the main findings? An airborne bio-radar system to remotely sense vital signs of survivors for post-disaster search and rescue was developed.Theoretical analysis of the impact of interference coming from the motion of the UAV platform and echoes from the background environment on radar detection performance. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-12642142.title: Aortic pseudoaneurysm as a rare complication of purulent pericarditis: case report and literature review
pmc-12642142.creator: Chun-Yu Yueh, Ming-Li Li, Ching-Feng Wu
pmc-12642142.description: BackgroundPurulent pericarditis has become rare in the antibiotic era, particularly when complicated by secondary infections such as an aortic pseudoaneurysm.Case presentationWe report a 46-year-old man who presented with persistent chest pain and cold sweats for three days. Imaging revealed a large pericardial effusion, and cultures grew methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus(MRSA).

pmc-12670688.title: Evaluation of a Community-Based Advance Care Planning Campaign for a General Adult Population
pmc-12670688.creator: Peiyuan Zhang, Tiffany C Erbelding, Glenn E Schneider, Nikki Highsmith Vernick, John G Cagle
pmc-12670688.description: Background:Early advance care planning (ACP) has been widely recommended, but overall uptake remains low. Most efforts to improve formal ACP adoption, namely living will (LW) and health care agent (HCA) documentation, focus on medical settings targeted at older adults with serious or chronic illness, while community-based ACP campaigns are limited.

pmc-13093671.title: Evaluation of Cerebral Blood Flow and Cerebral Autoregulation Using Synthetic Data and In Silico Modeling
pmc-13093671.creator: Selim Bozkurt
pmc-13093671.description: AimsThe classic view of static cerebral autoregulatory function suggests that cerebral blood flow (CBF) remains relatively stable across a wide range of mean arterial pressure (MAP). Recent studies propose a narrow autoregulatory range, as the methods used to manipulate MAP may also influence CBF.

pmc-13106199.title: The M.A.G.I.C. framework for mHealth development: applying game design principles from ‘Magic: The Gathering’
pmc-13106199.creator: James Broussard, Jana Fleet, Joseph McBride, Shanteria Brock, Joanne LeBrun, Monica Miller, Edelgard Wulfert
pmc-13106199.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). With the rapid advancement of digital health technologies, developers and behavioral health experts are increasingly exploring unconventional methods to modernize technology-based clinical interventions. The primary aim of this paper is to outline game design principles and lessons described by the developers of Magic: The Gathering (MTG), one of the world’s most popular and enduring fantasy role-playing card games, and explore how these tenets can be used to enhance mHealth (including wellness apps, wearable devices, and digital therapeutics).

pmc-13202950.title: Efficacy and safety of remimazolam for sedation of patients with end-stage renal disease: a prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial
pmc-13202950.creator: Jie Gao, Hong Yu, Zhao Xu, Yongqing Xu, Yuwei Wu, Peng Liang
pmc-13202950.description: BackgroundProcedural sedation in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) is challenging due to impaired renal function, which affects drug metabolism and increases the risk of adverse events. Remimazolam, a novel ultrashort-acting intravenous sedative, offers rapid onset and clearance independent of renal function, making it a potential alternative to dexmedetomidine for sedation in this patient population.

pmc-13401698.title: Coaches' and Parents' Perception Regarding Special Olympics' Commitment to the Promotion of Sport for Athletes With Intellectual Disabilities: A Cross‐Sectional Study

pmc-13499417.title: Growth rate, diameter at rupture, and associated patient characteristics of abdominal aortic aneurysms without an intraluminal thrombus
pmc-13499417.creator: Moritz Lindquist Liljeqvist, Asta Joshi, Antti Siika, Marko Bogdanovic, Patricia Andersson, Stefan Stoisavljevic, Rebecka Hultgren, Joy Roy
pmc-13499417.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to provide clinical and prognostic data on the small share of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) devoid of an intraluminal thrombus (ILT).MethodsThree retrospective samples were studied: electively treated patients (n = 234, growth rates available for n = 158 and an early baseline computed tomography [CT] available for n = 128), patients with rupture (n = 133), and those followed in surveillance (n = 161).

pmc-13518127.title: Orbital asymmetry degree: a potential 99mTc-DTPA SPECT/CT imaging marker for diplopia in thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy
pmc-13518127.creator: Xiaoan Pang, Jing Liang, Ziquan Zhou, Hengzhang Liang, Chen Yang, Zhixiao Wei
pmc-13518127.description: BackgroundDiplopia is a common and clinically important manifestation of thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), often related to asymmetric orbital involvement. This study investigated the association between orbital asymmetry degree (OAD), a novel quantitative imaging index derived from 99mTc-DTPA SPECT/CT, and diplopia in patients with TAO.MethodsA1:1 matched case–control study was conducted, including 22 matched pairs of patients with TAO with or without diplopia.

pmc-13628833.title: Oral PrEP pause and restart among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) who initiated PrEP in an HIV prevention program in Kampala, Uganda: a qualitative study
pmc-13628833.creator: Lazaaro Mujumbusi, Ivy Kayesu, Zam Nabalwanyi, Yunia Mayanja
pmc-13628833.description: IntroductionThere is interest in PrEP uptake amongst young people at high risk of HIV. However, there is a significant decline in PrEP starting from three to six months after PrEP initiation, thus affecting PrEP persistence and continuation due to pausing and stopping of PrEP, with a few restarting it.

uslaw-usc-t38-s5905.title: 38 U.S.C. § 5905 — Penalty for certain acts
uslaw-usc-t38-s5905.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t38-s5905.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part IV (General Administrative Provisions); Chapter 59 (Agents And Attorneys). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever wrongfully withholds from any claimant or beneficiary any part of a benefit or claim allowed and due to the claimant or beneficiary, shall be fined as provided in title 18, or imprisoned not more than one year, or both.
